arxiv-1809-01427.title: Covariance and Contravariance: a fresh look at an old issue (a primer in advanced type systems for learning functional programmers)
arxiv-1809-01427.creator: Giuseppe Castagna
arxiv-1809-01427.description: Abstract . Twenty years ago, in an article titled “Covariance and contravariance: conflict without a cause”, I argued that covariant and contravariant specialization of method parameters in object-oriented programming had different purposes and deduced that, not only they could, but actually they should both coexist in the same language.

arxiv-1909-08713.title: Homogenization of quadratic convolution energies in periodically perforated domains
arxiv-1909-08713.creator: Andrea Braides, Andrey Piatnitski
arxiv-1909-08713.description: Abstract Abstract. We prove a homogenization theorem for quadratic convolution energies defined in perforated domains. The corresponding limit is a Dirichlet-type quadratic energy, whose integrand is defined by a non-local cell-problem formula. The proof relies on an extension theorem from perforated domains belonging to a wide class containing compact periodic perforations. Keywords.

arxiv-1910-04269.title: Spoken Language Identification using ConvNets
arxiv-1910-04269.creator: Sarthak, Shikhar Shukla, Govind Mittal
arxiv-1910-04269.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Sarthak, Shikhar Shukla, Govind Mittal. Language Identification (LI) is an important first step in several speech processing systems. With a growing number of voice-based assistants, speech LI has emerged as a widely researched field. To approach the problem of identifying languages, we can either adopt an implicit approach where only the speech for a language is present or an explicit one where text is available with its corresponding transcript. This paper focuses on an implicit approach due to the absence of transcriptive data.

arxiv-2005-05134.title: On oriented planar trees with three leaves
arxiv-2005-05134.creator: Jack Morava
arxiv-2005-05134.description: Abstract . This elementary note proposes candidates for interesting continuous piecewise-smooth ‘Riemannian’ metrics on the moduli spaces of rooted geodesic trees embedded in the Poincaré disk. A related digression observes the existence of an apparently hitherto unrecognized abelian topological group structure on the real projective line. This is an early draft.

arxiv-2007-10354.title: On matrix models and their q q -deformations Preprint: UUITP-25/20 arXiv: 2007.10354
arxiv-2007-10354.creator: Luca Cassia, Rebecca Lodin, and Maxim Zabzine
arxiv-2007-10354.description: Abstract Motivated by the BPS/CFT correspondence, we explore the similarities between the classical β \beta -deformed Hermitean matrix model and the q q -deformed matrix models associated to 3d 𝒩 = 2 \mathcal{N}=2 supersymmetric gauge theories on D 2 × q S 1 D^{2}\times_{q}S^{1} and S b 3 S_{b}^{3} by matching parameters of the theories.

arxiv-2201-09424.title: An Effective Iterated Two-stage Heuristic Algorithm for the Multiple Traveling Salesmen Problem
arxiv-2201-09424.creator: Jiongzhi Zheng, Yawei Hong, Wenchang Xu, Wentao Li, Yongfu Chen
arxiv-2201-09424.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Jiongzhi Zheng, Yawei Hong, Wenchang Xu, Wentao Li, Yongfu Chen. The multiple Traveling Salesmen Problem ( m m TSP) is a general extension of the famous NP-hard Traveling Salesmen Problem (TSP), that there are m m ( m > 1 m>1 ) salesmen to visit the cities.

arxiv-2209-08805.title: Generalized derivations and generalized exponential monomials on hypergroups
arxiv-2209-08805.creator: Żywilla Fechner, Eszter Gselmann, László Székelyhidi
arxiv-2209-08805.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Żywilla Fechner, Eszter Gselmann, László Székelyhidi. In one of our former papers Endomorphisms of the measure algebra of commutative hypergroups ( arXiv:2204.07499 ) we considered exponential monomials on hypergroups and higher order derivations of the corresponding measure algebra. Continuing with this, we are now looking for the connection between the generalized exponential polynomials of a commutative hypergroup and the higher order derivations of the corresponding measure algebra.

arxiv-2211-16197.title: FJMP: Factorized Joint Multi-Agent Motion Prediction over Learned Directed Acyclic Interaction Graphs
arxiv-2211-16197.creator: Luke Rowe, Martin Ethier, Eli-Henry Dykhne, Krzysztof Czarnecki
arxiv-2211-16197.description: Abstract Predicting the future motion of road agents is a critical task in an autonomous driving pipeline. In this work, we address the problem of generating a set of scene-level, or joint, future trajectory predictions in multi-agent driving scenarios. To this end, we propose FJMP, a Factorized Joint Motion Prediction framework for multi-agent interactive driving scenarios.

arxiv-2306-03781.title: Imitation dynamics on networks with incomplete information
arxiv-2306-03781.creator: Xiaochen Wang 1,† , Lei Zhou 2,† , Alex McAvoy 3,4 , Aming Li 1,5,∗ 1 Center for Systems and Control, College of Engineering, Peking University, Beijing 100871, China 2 School of Automation, Beijing Institute of Technology, Beijing 100081, China 3 School of Data Science and Society, University of No
arxiv-2306-03781.description: Abstract Imitation is an important learning heuristic in animal and human societies. Previous explorations report that the fate of individuals with cooperative strategies is sensitive to the protocol of imitation, leading to a conundrum about how different styles of imitation quantitatively impact the evolution of cooperation.

arxiv-2312-06648.title: EMNLP 2024 Main Conference Dense 𝕏 \mathbb{X} Retrieval: What Retrieval Granularity Should We Use?
arxiv-2312-06648.creator: Tong Chen Hongwei Wang Sihao Chen Wenhao Yu, Kaixin Ma Xinran Zhao Hongming Zhang Dong Yu
arxiv-2312-06648.description: Abstract Dense retrieval has become a prominent method to obtain relevant context or world knowledge in open-domain NLP tasks. When we use a learned dense retriever on a retrieval corpus at inference time, an often-overlooked design choice is the retrieval unit in which the corpus is indexed, e.g. document, passage, or sentence.

arxiv-2404-08099.title: Comparing quantum fluctuations in the spin- 1 2 \frac{1}{2} and spin- 1 1 XXZ Heisenberg models on square and honeycomb lattices
arxiv-2404-08099.creator: Masahiro Kadosawa, Masaaki Nakamura, Yukinori Ohta, Satoshi Nishimoto
arxiv-2404-08099.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Masahiro Kadosawa, Masaaki Nakamura, Yukinori Ohta, Satoshi Nishimoto. We present a detailed investigation of the XXZ Heisenberg model for spin- 1 / 2 1/2 and spin- 1 1 systems on square and honeycomb lattices. Utilizing the density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) method, complemented by Spiral Boundary Conditions (SBC) for mapping two-dimensional (2D) clusters onto one-dimensional (1D) chains, we meticulously explore the evolution of staggered magnetization and spin gaps across a broad spectrum of easy-axis anisotropies.

arxiv-2502-20731.title: Indoor Localization for Autonomous Robot Navigation
arxiv-2502-20731.creator: Sean Kouma, Rachel Masters
arxiv-2502-20731.description: Abstract Indoor positioning systems (IPS’s) have gained attention as outdoor navigation becomes prevalent in everyday life. Research is being actively conducted on how indoor smartphone navigation can be accomplished and improved using received signal strength indication (RSSI) and machine learning (ML).

arxiv-2506-22966.title: Detection of coordinated fleet vehicles in route choice urban games. Part I. Inverse fleet assignment theory.
arxiv-2506-22966.creator: Grzegorz Jamróz ∗, Rafał Kucharski
arxiv-2506-22966.description:
A 2025 arXiv research paper by Grzegorz Jamróz ∗, Rafał Kucharski. Abstract:
Detection of collectively routing fleets of vehicles in future urban systems may become important for the management of traffic, as such routing may destabilize urban networks leading to deterioration of driving conditions. Accordingly, in this paper we discuss the question whether it is possible to determine the flow of fleet vehicles on all routes given the fleet size and behaviour as well as the combined total flow of fleet and non-fleet vehicles on every route.

arxiv-2509-17763.title: Reduced fluctuations: Surprising effects of noise cross correlations in a coupled, driven model
arxiv-2509-17763.creator: Sudip Mukherjee
arxiv-2509-17763.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Sudip Mukherjee. We elucidate how the strong coupling phases of a coupled driven model, originally proposed in S. E 108 , 024219 (2023), are affected by noise cross correlations in general dimensions d d . This model has two dynamical variables, where one of the variables is autonomous being independent of the other, whereas the second one depends explicitly on the former. By employing model coupling theories, we study the strong coupling phase of model.

pmc-10572400.title: Inhibition Mechanism of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum on the Growth and Biogenic Amine Production in Morganella morganii
pmc-10572400.creator: Zhenxiao Sun, Yi Zhang, Xinping Lin, Sufang Zhang, Yingxi Chen, Chaofan Ji, Artur Roig-Sagués
pmc-10572400.description: Morganella morganii, a spoilage bacterium in fermented foods, produces harmful biogenic amines (BAs). Although Lactiplantibacillus plantarum is widely used to inhibit spoilage bacteria, the inhibition pattern and inhibition mechanism of M. morganii by Lpb. plantarum are not well studied. In this study, we analysed the effects of the addition of Lpb.

pmc-10600097.title: Prognostic impact of translocation t(14;16) in multiple myeloma according to the presence of additional genetic lesions
pmc-10600097.creator: Anaïs Schavgoulidze, Aurore Perrot, Titouan Cazaubiel, Xavier Leleu, Lydia Montes, Caroline Jacquet, Karim Belhadj, Sabine Brechignac, Laurent Frenzel, Thomas Chalopin, Philippe Rey, Jean-Marc Schiano de Collela, Mamoun Dib, Denis Caillot, Margaret Macro, Jean Fontan, Laure Buisson, Luka Pavageau, M
pmc-10600097.description: Avet-Loiseau, Jill Corre Published: 2023 Patients with multiple myeloma (MM) have experienced a markedly improved survival over the past 25 years, thanks in part to the availability of new drugs [1]. However, a subgroup of patients known as high-risk patients continues to represent an unmet medical need, with an overall survival of less than three years [2].

pmc-10663748.title: Breast cancer therapies reduce risk of Alzheimer’s disease and promote estrogenic pathways and action in brain
pmc-10663748.creator: Gregory L. Branigan, Georgina Torrandell-Haro, Shuhua Chen, Yuan Shang, Samantha Perez-Miller, Zisu Mao, Marco Padilla-Rodriguez, Helena Cortes-Flores, Francesca Vitali, Roberta Diaz Brinton
pmc-10663748.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). SummaryWorldwide, an ever-increasing number of women are prescribed estrogen-modulating therapies (EMTs) for the treatment of breast cancer. In parallel, aging of the global population of women will contribute to risk of both breast cancer and Alzheimer’s disease. To address the impact of anti-estrogen therapies on risk of Alzheimer’s and neural function, we conducted medical informatic and molecular pharmacology analyses to determine the impact of EMTs on risk of Alzheimer’s followed by determination of EMT estrogenic mechanisms of action in neurons.

pmc-11324783.title: “As a patient I do not belong to the clinic, I belong to the community”: co-developing multi-level, person-centred tuberculosis stigma interventions in Cape Town, South Africa
pmc-11324783.creator: Sally E Hayward, Nosivuyile Vanqa, Goodman Makanda, Phumeza Tisile, Luthando Ngwatyu, Isabel Foster, Abenathi A Mcinziba, Amanda Biewer, Rachel Mbuyamba, Michelle Galloway, Siyavuya Bunyula, Helene-Mari van der Westhuizen, Jon S Friedland, Andrew Medina-Marino, Lario Viljoen, Ingrid Schoeman, Graeme
pmc-11324783.description: BackgroundAnticipated, internal, and enacted stigma are major barriers to tuberculosis (TB) care engagement and directly impact patient well-being. Unfortunately, targeted stigma interventions are lacking. We aimed to co-develop a person-centred stigma intervention with TB-affected community members and health workers in South Africa.

pmc-11402218.title: The direct and indirect pathways of the basal ganglia antagonistically influence cortical activity and perceptual decisions
pmc-11402218.creator: Enny H van Beest, Mohammed AO Abdelwahab, J Leonie Cazemier, Chrysiida Baltira, M Cassandra Maes, Brandon D Peri, Matthew W Self, Ingo Willuhn, Pieter R Roelfsema
pmc-11402218.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). SummaryThe striatum, the main input nucleus of the basal ganglia, receives topographically organized input from the cortex and gives rise to the direct and indirect output pathways, which have antagonistic effects on basal ganglia output directed to the cortex. We optogenetically stimulated the direct and indirect pathways in a visual and a working memory task in mice that responded by licking. Unilateral direct pathway stimulation increased the probability of lick responses toward the contralateral, non-stimulated side and increased cortical activity globally.

pmc-11422740.title: Prompt Engineering Paradigms for Medical Applications: Scoping Review
pmc-11422740.creator: Jamil Zaghir, Marco Naguib, Mina Bjelogrlic, Aurélie Névéol, Xavier Tannier, Christian Lovis
pmc-11422740.description: BackgroundPrompt engineering, focusing on crafting effective prompts to large language models (LLMs), has garnered attention for its capabilities at harnessing the potential of LLMs. This is even more crucial in the medical domain due to its specialized terminology and language technicity. Clinical natural language processing applications must navigate complex language and ensure privacy compliance.

pmc-11431339.title: Stress among Nursing Students in the Era of the COVID-19 Pandemic
pmc-11431339.creator: Grzegorz Kobelski, Katarzyna Naylor, Aleksandra Kobelska, Mariusz Wysokiński, Alessia Verduri
pmc-11431339.description: Introduction: The COVID-19 pandemic has significantly impacted stress levels across various professions, particularly in the medical field. This increase in stress has also affected medical students, including nursing students, who faced unprecedented and challenging circumstances. Nursing students, in particular, experienced added pressure due to observing the frontline experiences of nurses and the new demands placed upon them.

pmc-11688531.title: Out of and in East Asia: phylogeny, biogeography and diversification of Thalictroideae (Ranunculaceae) in the Northern Hemisphere
pmc-11688531.creator: Yuan-Yuan Ling, Huan-Wen Peng, Lian Lian, Andrey S Erst, Kun-Li Xiang, Wei Wang
pmc-11688531.description: Background and AimsUnderstanding the biogeographical patterns and processes underlying the distribution of diversity within the Northern Hemisphere has fascinated botanists and biogeographers for over a century. However, as a well-known centre of species diversity in the Northern Hemisphere, whether East Asia acted as a source and/or a sink of plant diversity of the Northern Hemisphere remains unclear.

pmc-12437697.title: Is There a Burnout Epidemic among Medical Students?
pmc-12437697.creator: M Di Vincenzo
pmc-12437697.description: AbstractMedical students are persistently exposed to specific conditions that may have detrimental effects on mental health, such as stressful academic routine, demanding and heterogeneous curriculum, sense of competition and daily exposure to illness and death. Accumulating evidence highlights high levels of cynicism and emotional exhaustion among these subjects.

pmc-12455507.title: Antibiotic resistance and factors associated with colonization dynamics of Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus pneumoniae in healthy children in Lima, Peru
pmc-12455507.creator: Valeria Mariana Li Valverde, Paulo Cesar Aguirre Castañeda, Brayan E Gonzales, Franco Castillo-Tokumori, Jorge E Vidal, Theresa J Ochoa
pmc-12455507.description: Pneumococcal conjugate vaccines (PCVs) have influenced population dynamics of Streptococcus pneumoniae in the nasopharynx and may have contributed to increased Staphylococcus aureus colonization. This study assessed the prevalence of colonization, antibiotic resistance patterns, and associated risk factors for colonization and co-colonization of S. aureus and S. pneumoniae in healthy Peruvian children post-PCV introduction.

pmc-12744724.title: Proteomics-based multi-omics reveals m6A-mediated regulation of the plant proteome
pmc-12744724.creator: Sheng Fan, Lisha Shen
pmc-12744724.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). pments are transforming our ability to dissect complex regulatory networks and are increasingly being integrated into multi-omics frameworks for gene discovery and trait analysis. Notably, two recent studies have produced the most comprehensive pan-tissue, proteomics-centered multi-omics atlases to date in rice and soybean—two of the world’s most important crops—revealing a key role for N⁶-methyladenosine (m6A) in the post-transcriptional regulation of the plant proteome (Li et al., 2024; Yang et al., 2025).

pmc-13221877.title: Paroxysmal Pause-Dependent Atrioventricular Block
pmc-13221877.creator: Timothy Nathan Kwan, Hariharan Raju, Jamie Cham, Harry Mond, Raymond W. Sy
pmc-13221877.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundPause-dependent atrioventricular (AV) block is a cause of syncope and cardiac arrest characterized by abrupt but transient conduction failure with ventricular standstill despite previous AV conduction. It is frequently under-recognized.Case SummaryWe describe 4 patients presenting with syncope. Baseline electrocardiograms were nondiagnostic, but continuous monitoring captured episodes of sudden high-grade AV block initiated by pauses or premature beats, without progressive PR prolongation.

pmc-13323627.title: Case Report: Malignant transformation of deep infiltrating endometriosis: a report of two cases and literature review
pmc-13323627.creator: Yue Gu, Xuanxuan Zhao, Yongheng Shi, Zhijun Hu, Qing Liu, Hong Zhu, Peiquan Li, Kaijiang Liu

pmc-13603697.title: Antimicrobial Resistance and Associated Genetic Determinants of Aliivibrio Colonizing the Gastrointestinal Tract of Farmed Atlantic Salmon (Salmo salar L.)
pmc-13603697.creator: Josephine K. Hamlett, John P. Bowman
pmc-13603697.description: Background/Objectives: Currently, readily available data on antimicrobial resistance in bacteria colonizing farmed Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar L.) are limited. Recent data indicate that the gastrointestinal tract mucosa of adult Atlantic salmon farmed in Tasmania (Australia) is consistently colonized by Aliivibrio species. Aliivibrio and other Vibrionaceae may contribute to gut dysbiosis through overgrowth.
